inspected_anchors.anchor: Symbolic states, preconditions/effects, inferred goals and ambiguity formulation.
Candidate goals, confidence and margin thresholds, and clarification as a state transition.
Algorithm and task construction: four request types and a controlled 120-task suite.
Deterministic mocked execution, comparator definitions, metric definitions and aggregate results.
Six-method aggregate results and distinction between wrong goals and tool selection.
Request-type regression, unnecessary clarification, token cost, Nova replacement and final-row error analysis.
Controlled benchmark limitations, noisy users, changing APIs, open-world goals and clarification assumptions.
Latency, monetary cost and user satisfaction remain unmeasured; artifact availability statement.

supported_claims: Tool discovery/filtering assumes a symbolic target goal; goal inference and downstream path filtering are separate tasks.
Clarification can be represented as a state transition; it is a design for controlled preconditions/effects, not an identified causal estimand.
Author-reported 97.0% success versus80.1% top-goal CMTF and2.5% versus19.4% wrong-goal rates are conditional on120 controlled tasks and deterministic mocked tool execution.
Reported explicit requests show lower GIST success than semantic-goal filtering and 16.8% unnecessary clarification; ambiguity handling trades friction for wrong-goal reduction.
The original explicitly lists noisy users, evolving APIs, nondeterministic effects, open-world goals, real users, latency and monetary cost as unresolved.
limitations: A single arXiv v1 is reviewed, not peer accepted or independently reproduced.
The paper maps user text to symbolic goals and action/tool transitions; it does not construct or validate a banking causal DAG or effect.

supported_claims: Pinned runner forces clarification for annotated nonexplicit request types and substitutes intended_goal after the clarification action; this is not a real user-turn evaluation.
Pinned runner reads gold_path while all120 saved task objects contain gold_chains and no gold_path; paper metric replay cannot be asserted from this runner plus inputs.
Released final CSV has5040 unique positive-token rows; 53/560 nonexplicit GIST rows show zero clarifications. Paper aggregate tables reproduce from that CSV, not from fresh model calls.
Run CSV has fields absent from the runner writer and lacks writer fields; a separate producer/transform or revision remains possible.
Cutoff default model list names Nova 2 Pro preview while saved final data uses Nova Pro; an explicit override is possible but not retained in inspected artifacts.
MIT source notice is explicit; the six package requirements are unpinned. Latency, costs, users, real APIs, multi-turn clarification and full provider-failure denominator are not established.
limitations: Primary paper reports results; source inconsistency leaves producer/cleaning provenance open, not a fabrication finding.
No upstream code or model call executed.
No arbitrary causal diagram discovery, statistical identification, bank benefit or live-client integration is established.
